title: Borrowing, References, Slices & Lifetimes
objectives: Use shared (&T) and exclusive (&mut T) borrows correctly
Slice strings and collections without copying
body:
# Borrowing, References, Slices & Lifetimes

## Two kinds of borrow — enforced everywhere

```rust
fn length(text: &String) -> usize { text.len() }   // shared: many OK
fn push_bang(text: &mut String) { text.push('!'); } // exclusive: one only
```

The rules:
- Any number of `&T` **or** exactly one `&mut T` at a time.
- Owner must outlive every borrower.

This kills data races *at compile time*.

## Slices borrow a view

```rust
let word = String::from("happiness");
let happy = &word[0..5];      // &str view into the buffer — zero copy
let all: &str = &word;        // deref coercion String → &str
let nums = [1, 2, 3, 4];
let tail: &[i32] = &nums[2..];
```

Prefer `&str` parameters over `&String`, `&[T]` over `&Vec<T>` — accept the
most general borrowed form (the newtype of good API design).

## Lifetimes in signatures

Mostly inferred; needed when two inputs are involved:

```rust
fn longest<'a>(a: &'a str, b: &'a str) -> &'a str {
    if a.len() > b.len() { a } else { b }
}
```

Read `'a` as: *the returned reference lives no longer than both inputs*.
The compiler checks callers against this contract. Don't sprinkle lifetimes
where inference works — unnecessary annotations are their own smell.
